messages:
sasha: paging alert — we are seeing a KV-cache blowup on the AWQ int8 path for model:open-llama-13b-awq. tail latency and 5xxs spiked ~10:41 UTC, customers X and ACME hit errors. raising page to incidents.
incident-bot: New incident created: #INC-2025-328 — KV cache / quantization regression affecting continuous batching. Paging metric exceeded threshold. Pager: eng-oncall.
eng-oncall: I'm on it. grabbing logs and tracing cache usage. can someone post the affected model list and any recent deploys?
sasha: recent rollout: runtime kernel selector change (~2h ago) that added a new awq-int8 kernel candidate. also a continuous-batching tweak (batcher:increase-prefix-tolerance=true) merged yesterday. suspect interaction.
kai: checked the metrics — KV_CACHE_ENTRIES for open-llama-13b-awq jumped from ~200k -> 540k within 30m. swap I/O spiked on gpu-nodes-3/4, paging started at 10:38.
ops_josh: customer ACME reports requests timing out, they saw 503s and slow tokens. I have a support ticket open (TKT-1129) and notified their SE.
maria: quick mitigation plan: 1) disable AWQ int8 quant path at runtime (fallback to gptq/fp16), 2) reduce continuous-batcher max_tokens to 256 to shrink in-flight KV growth, 3) evict KV cache for the affected model, 4) roll workers with new env. wanna run steps in that order?
eng-oncall: agree. Kai — can you push a control-plane override to prefer gptq for that model? I'll start a temporary batcher config rollback.
kai: pushing override now. command: ```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://controlplane.redwood.io/v1/models/open-llama-13b-awq/override" -d '{"quant_preference":"gptq","kernel_policy":"disable_awq_int8"}'
```
infra-bot: override accepted — model open-llama-13b-awq now has policy quant_preference=gptq. propagation to edge routing will take ~30s.
eng-oncall: reducing batcher config on the fleet: setting REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256 and REDWOOD_BATCH_PREFIX_TOLERANCE=0.25 via config service. command: ```
rbctl set-config batcher REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256 REDWOOD_BATCH_PREFIX_TOLERANCE=0.25 --scope=fleet
```
sasha: while that propagates, please evict KV cache for the model to free memory ASAP. use admin endpoint to clear entries without a full restart if possible.
kai: evict API called: ```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.io/cache/evict" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b-awq","scope":"kv_cache"}'
```
infra-bot: cache-evict job queued on gpu-nodes-3..5. estimated completion 45s.
ops_josh: ACME latency dropping already? their telemetry shows p95 down from 7.2s -> 3.1s after override propagated (~10:44). still some 5xxs but decreasing.
eng-oncall: rolling restart of batcher workers on nodes 3..5 to pick up env changes. command: ```
for n in 3 4 5; do ssh gpu-node-$n 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-batcher && echo restarted $n'; done
```
maria: note — the root cause hypothesis: AWQ int8 kernel encodes KV keys/values with a different block size leading to ~2x KV footprint vs gptq. combined with the new batching tolerance (which allowed longer prefix merges) the cache grew non-linearly and hit swap. need long-term: kernel metrics + unit test for KV sizing across quant paths.
eng-oncall: confirmation — after cache evict + override + batcher rollback, swap I/O returned to baseline and 5xx rate dropped to normal over 3m. monitoring: keep an eye for re-growth.
ops_josh: sent customer update to ACME + flagged next steps with their SE. They marked incident as "degraded" -> now "mitigated" on their side.
cust-success-elaine: ACME appreciated the quick mitigation, asked for a postmortem and a plan to avoid repeat. noted SLA credit request if recurrence.
sasha: capturing follow-ups: 1) create regression test that measures KV cache per-model per-quant-path, 2) add a warning in runtime when KV entries grow >300k within 15m, 3) revert the kernel selector change until we validate KV footprint on AWQ-INT8, 4) add e2e eval with continuous-batching toggled.
kai: opened jira INC-3295 with the above tasks and assigned to eng-runtime + eng-ml.
eng-oncall: final status — incident mitigated at 10:49 UTC. will keep the overrides until the kernel change is validated and tests are in place. scheduling a bridge for 14:00 UTC postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2025-328 status updated: mitigated. bridge scheduled.
sasha: thanks everyone. followup: please include KV size histogram and kernel memory encoding docs in the postmortem. Also add a canary test that exercises awq-int8 on small models before fleet rollout. :thumbsup:
